title: Daily camera-trap detections of 47 bird and mammal taxa at 146 cameras on private land in three West Virginia county pairs, April-September 2022
creator: Rota, Christopher T.; Pesi, Sarah M.
citation: Rota, C. T. (2023). Data for White-tailed Deer Detection Intensity Increases When Coyotes Are Present [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5061/zenodo.10391650

intellectualRights.note: Zenodo record CC BY 4.0; every row of sequences.csv (Wildlife Insights export) carries licence CC-BY-NC, which governs

abstract: Game cameras deployed for about two months in summer 2022 at 146 sites on private land in Jackson-Mason, Barbour-Upshur and Hampshire counties, West Virginia, one of three camera datasets Clipp et al. (2024) combined to fit a two-species occupancy model with a continuous-time detection process for white-tailed deer and coyote. The Wildlife Insights sequence export lists every identified sequence, so this table carries all 47 taxa identified to species (wild and domestic mammals and birds) as daily detection/non-detection with the number of sequences, with camera coordinates as published.
samplingProtocol: Game cameras on private land, deployed 1.7-76 days (median 62) between 2022-04-23 and 2022-09-15; images grouped into sequences (photos within one minute of each other) and identified in Wildlife Insights. Occasion = calendar day of the deployment; effort = hours the camera operated within that day, from the deployment and retrieval timestamps.
closureNote: occasion (camera-days within one deployment of up to 76 days, the paper's closure assumption); no period
geographicCoverage: Private land in Jackson, Mason, Barbour, Upshur and Hampshire counties, West Virginia, USA (camera coordinates as published)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: none: no taxon is flagged (no IUCN CR/EN/VU species; white-tailed deer and coyote are Least Concern); coordinates as deposited

notShipped.out_of_window: 265 sequences timestamped outside their deployment window: 199 with a wrong camera year (2017, 2021) at four cameras whose comments report clock faults, 66 at the deployment or retrieval boundary (61 by under an hour, 5 by 2-12 hours)
notShipped.higher-rank, human, vehicle, insect labe: sequences not identified to a bird or mammal species (Unknown, Animal, Mammal, Rodent, Sciurus Species, Human-*, Vehicle, Insect, ...)
notShipped.group_size, age, sex: per-sequence attributes that do not survive aggregation to camera-days
notShipped.sites.RDS ndvi: per-camera NDVI the authors computed from 30 m rasters; not among the deposited raw files
notShipped.wtd.RDS, coy.RDS, stan_data.RDS, Fitted-: derived from the detections; model inputs and outputs
notShipped.Data/SNAPSHOT_USA_2020_*.csv: the full Snapshot USA 2020 release re-uploaded by the authors (third-party data, not hosted from this deposit)
notShipped.Data/Wildlife_Openings_*.csv: the 2019-2021 Monongahela cameras, shipped as clipp_2024_monongahela_comm

notes: Eight Jackson-Mason deployments (sheet rows 46-53, units JacksonMason_46..53) are in the deployment sheet and the sequence export but were not modelled in the paper (no NDVI); __units.modelled_in_paper marks them. Fourteen cameras were not working at retrieval; the deposit does not say when they failed, so their later camera-days may overstate effort (unit_camera_working_at_retrieval). Deployment names in the deposit are property-owner surnames plus a camera number; unit is pseudonymised to <county-pair>_<sheet row> and the names are not shipped.
